description: OpenClaw profile extracted from LawyerRAG's director/orchestra runtime.
extraInstructions: Strictly adhere to the established project coding standards in AGENTS.md.
Ensure all new features are covered by E2E tests in the relevant lane.

operatorDirective: Keep LawyerRAG-specific behavior in the installed profile and repo-local control-plane artifacts, not in the shared runtime.
Use `.openclaw/program.md` to steer adoption, lane ownership, and migration sequencing before touching framework internals.
Treat `.openclaw/recipes/README.md` as the editable surface for repo-specific prompts, sweeps, and reviewer handoff rules.

recipeSeeds.title: Lane-Safe Backend Change
recipeSeeds.whenToUse: Use when a backend change affects contracts, verification commands, or reviewer handoff expectations.
steps: Read the installed profile plus the relevant backend reading rules before editing.
Update canonical contracts and dependent tests together.
Preserve audit and orchestration artifacts when changing queue or sweep behavior.

recipeSeeds.title: UI Route Change
recipeSeeds.whenToUse: Use when route-level UI work touches the reports frontend, audits, or frontend lane docs.
steps: Read the active frontend lane docs and UI design principles first.
Keep route verification commands aligned with the selected lane.
Document new repo-specific workflow rules here instead of patching installer internals.

extensionPoints.summary: Import another repo shape by adding a new profile package and detection signals.
extensionPoints.delivery: Add `profiles/<profile-id>/profile.json` plus fixture-backed installer coverage instead of branching on LawyerRAG.

extensionPoints.summary: Extend session, tracing, or provider capabilities without changing lane policy code.
extensionPoints.delivery: Add or update a thin adapter package and keep capability routing in profile data.

extensionPoints.summary: Adopt orchestration or audit ideas from sibling repos through explicit proposals and tests.
extensionPoints.delivery: Capture the source repo and adopted idea in the framework map, then add targeted runtime or installer tests.

manualSteps: Connect the required local model providers and repo secrets before running dispatcher cycles.
Review repo-owned control-plane files under `.openclaw/` and keep them authoritative where they already exist.
Create a short proposal under `.openclaw/proposals/` before changing sweeps, promotion rules, or lane ownership semantics.

coreRuntime.summary: Extract the LawyerRAG director loop into a generic runtime that seeds work, enforces lane ownership, and runs sweeps via profile data.
inheritedFromLawyerRag: Queue refresh, stale run recovery, and promotion sweep behavior from scripts/openclaw_director.py.
Lane-bounded task packaging, required reading, and verification command selection from scripts/openclaw_director.py.
Manager persona defaults and seeded project continuity from scripts/openclaw_director.py.

adoptedIdeas: Append-only audit/event discipline should back director state transitions.
Heartbeat-oriented background processing should replace ad hoc sweep timing assumptions.
Deterministic workflow/operator trust patterns should inform queue state transitions.
Adapter session resume and compaction policy should be explicit runtime capability data.

outOfScope: LawyerRAG-specific file paths, lane names, and categories as framework defaults.
Hardcoded runtime table names beyond thin migration compatibility shims.

orchestraRuntimePlanning.summary: Retain LawyerRAG's artifact-producing Codex orchestra flow, but make planner policy and fan-out strategy generic.
inheritedFromLawyerRag: Prompt intake, promptify, plan, subtask, manifest, and reviewer handoff flow from scripts/codex_orchestra.py.
Machine-readable JSON artifacts for downstream review and promotion sweeps from scripts/codex_orchestra.py.

adoptedIdeas: Dependency-aware fan-out should be a first-class planner concern rather than a fixed chain of subtasks.
Orchestration logging should be preserved as a reusable artifact format.
Multi-agent planning should normalize work items before adapter execution.
A program.md-style human directive should constrain the runtime and explain keep/discard iteration rules.

outOfScope: Fixed subagent counts as a universal default.
Repo-specific prompt templates embedded into orchestra package code.

projectProfileSchema.summary: Profiles carry the repo-specific policy surface so the framework does not branch on LawyerRAG assumptions.
inheritedFromLawyerRag: Lane definitions, required-reading rules, verification rules, routing hints, manager state defaults, promotion policy, and artifact policy from scripts/openclaw_director.py.

adoptedIdeas: Operator-facing workflow defaults should be explicit profile data.
Transition discipline belongs in schema-visible policy, not in hidden runtime branches.
Major framework changes should be discussed openly and reflected in editable profile or docs artifacts.

outOfScope: Repo-local file naming conventions as package constants.
Implicit maintainer knowledge not represented in profile data.

memoryEval.summary: Memory and evaluation should be a reusable substrate for review, promotion, and harness improvement rather than a LawyerRAG-only embedding cache.
inheritedFromLawyerRag: Embeddings lifecycle, review artifacts, and queue refresh memory inputs from scripts/openclaw_director.py.

adoptedIdeas: Memory compression should be explicit policy, not only truncation.
Evaluation should be part of the runtime contract, not a separate afterthought.
Agent-to-agent and runtime abstractions should tolerate production deployment.
Verifier-first harness evolution and keep/discard experiment logic should inform runtime eval hooks.

outOfScope: Binding the framework to a single embedding provider or benchmark suite.

auditOps.summary: Operational trust should come from append-only logs, explicit state transitions, and public change process.
inheritedFromLawyerRag: Run events, task events, job runs, promotion artifacts, and stale-session cleanup expectations from scripts/openclaw_director.py.

adoptedIdeas: Append-only NDJSON audit logs with bounded retention.
Atomic transition/event discipline for operator trust.
Major architectural changes should follow an open review path rather than private runtime drift.

outOfScope: Repo-specific notification channels as mandatory framework behavior.

adapters.summary: Adapters stay thin, capability-declared, and replaceable so lane routing remains profile-driven.
inheritedFromLawyerRag: Codex/Gemini lane preference and thin executor boundaries currently encoded in the director/orchestra pair.

adoptedIdeas: Host-managed runtime identity and tracing should live at the adapter boundary.
Session management and compaction policy should be adapter-declared.
Tool/runtime abstractions should stay flexible enough for MCP and agent-to-agent use.

outOfScope: Adapter-specific queue, planning, or profile logic branches inside the core runtime.

installerAdoption.summary: Adoption should install a reusable framework with editable profile and directive files, not a frozen LawyerRAG transplant.
inheritedFromLawyerRag: Bootstrap runtime state, scheduled jobs, and manager seeds derived from the existing director runtime.

adoptedIdeas: Installer output should leave behind a human-readable program/directive document for operators.
Prompts, recipes, and extensions should remain openly editable after installation.

outOfScope: Permanent one-off migration code for LawyerRAG-specific runtime artifacts.

personas.name: Lawyer Legal Strategy
responsibilities: Ideate and review legal workflow improvements that improve evidence reasoning, court preparation, citations, and matter chronology.

Guard against unsupported legal claims and require provenance for user-facing legal reasoning.
decisionAuthority: Can prioritize legal workflow tasks inside LawyerRAG lanes.
Can require citation, provenance, or court-preparation acceptance criteria.
forbiddenActions: Weakening provenance, citation, or review evidence.

format: State the legal user outcome, source evidence, implementation scope, and verification.
Prefer matter, evidence, citation, and court-preparation language.
interactionRules: Create coherent feature slices that fit one PR.

verificationRules: Check provenance and citation behavior when user-facing legal text changes.

interactionRules: Prefer evidence-handling improvements over generic tests.
